hook_text: A ramp is 23 bags of cement, 19 metres of tube, eight days of work and three bakkie trips. Here is how you know.
clip_script: Every building job costs three things: materials, labour, transport. Materials come from the drawing: the ramp is 7.2 by 1.2 by 0.3, about 2.6 cubic metres of concrete, plus stairs and landing, call it 3.3. A cubic metre takes 7 bags of cement, half a metre of sand, half of stone. So 23 bags, 1.7 and 1.7. Rails: 19 metres of tube, 14 of posts. Prices come from the merchant, today, with the shop's name written down. Labour: a bricklayer and two workers, 8 days, at the local rate. Transport: deliveries. Add 10 percent for waste and 10 percent for surprises. Table it: item, quantity, price, total. Any line, anyone can check.
visual_style: Whiteboard ramp outline with dimensions becoming a volume; bags of cement stacking to 23; a five-column table filling; three labelled money bags for materials, labour and transport.
pacing: Three costs, the volume, the bags, the prices, the table, the allowances.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and price one bag of cement at your nearest hardware store.
